newsitem.title: BURUNDI: Burundi army arrests 14 students over protest.
newsitem.headline: Burundi army arrests 14 students over protest.

text.p: Burundi's army arrested 14 students on Wednesday during a university sit-in protest against military ruler Pierre Buyoya's decision to negotiate with Hutu rebels, eyewitnesses said.

The demonstration is part of a growing protest against Buyoya's announcement last week that his government signed a pre-ceasefire agreement with rebels from the National Council for the Defence of Democracy (CNDD) after secret talks in Rome.
Student banners read: "No negotiations with the genociders of CNDD" and "We demand the liberation of imprisoned students".

"Students are not convinced by the explanation given by Buyoya (for the talks). Even trade unionists disagree with him and ask him to stop the negotiations," said student leader Apollinaire Kavungirwa.
Twenty-three Burundian trade unions released a statement on Tuesday protesting over the negotiations and called on the elite civil society and population to take action if they continue.
Ethnic Tutsi Buyoya, who took power in a coup last July, said he entered negotiations in an effort to end a bitter civil war between the Tutsi-dominated army and rebels.
"The military supports the government initiative because its the best way toward peace and we support anything that can get peace in Burundi," said army spokesman Lieutenant-Colonel Isaie Nibizi.
Diplomats say they support the talks, but they are opposed by students, unionists and Tutsi politicians who fear ceding any power to CNDD compromises their security.
More than 150,000 people have been killed in Burundi since October 1993, when the country's first freely elected Hutu president was murdered in an attempted coup by Tutsi troops.
